criteria.criterion: event_of_job in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs reads the job's stored Verification and puts each unmet criterion's text and each blocker or major finding (severity, summary, location) into the Event's `what`; the field list in the module docs (and defaults-loop.md section 3.3 if it lists fields) names these additions.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: event_of_job appends verification_text(&job_records.verification) to `what`. verification_text lists unmet criteria with their kind and text, and blocker or major findings as 'severity at location: summary'. The module doc's field list, defaults-loop.md §3.3 ('Also reads, for a rejected or failed job') and decision-sets.md all name the additions.

criteria.criterion: A failed check (CheckRun with passed=false) is rendered in `what` under a separate, explicitly labelled 'failed checks' heading with its name and a bounded output_tail, never in the unmet-criteria list; the system prompt tells the model that criteria and checks are different things.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: failed checks go under their own section, 'Failed checks (tool runs such as fmt, clippy or test; they are not acceptance criteria)', with name, exit code and clip_end(output_tail, 800). The unmet list is built only from v.criteria. SYSTEM_PROMPT now says 'criteria and checks are different things, so never report a failed check as an unmet criterion'.

criteria.criterion: Added text is bounded (counts and character caps), redacted like the rest of the prompt, and still excludes transcripts, diffs and other jobs' files; a job with no verification.json (e.g. failed before verification) still produces the old `what`.
criteria.evidence: From reading the code: at most 6 items per section, 400 characters per text field and 800 characters of output tail. Only Verification fields are read. With `if let Some(verification)` unset, `what` stays as the old title-plus-reason text. On redaction: the user prompt is never redacted in introspect.rs; only the model's answer is (apply_answer, redact_all). Stored output_tail is redacted when written (checks.rs:197). So the new text gets the same treatment as the rest of the prompt, which holds as the criterion is worded.

criteria.criterion: New unit tests in introspect.rs cover: a rejection with one unmet criterion and a major finding (both appear in the prompt), a rejection whose only failure is a failed test check (appears as failed check, no unmet criterion), and a job without verification. Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`; `cargo test` passes, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean.
criteria.evidence: I ran `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`: 8 passed, including the 4 new tests. Two of the three required shapes are covered: an_unmet_criterion_and_a_major_finding_reach_the_prompt and a_failed_check_is_listed_apart_from_the_criteria. The third, 'a job without verification', is not. The nearest test, a_job_without_a_failure_in_its_verification_adds_nothing, uses a Verification that exists and has no failures. No test runs event_of_job with verification = None. In fact, no test calls event_of_job at all. Athena reports that the full test suite, clippy and fmt passed; I did not rerun them.

criteria.criterion: Outcome check for the steward: with the fake model, the user prompt for a rejected job built from a verification.json like that of job 20261014-170031-2r9b contains the text of the unmet criterion 8 and the major finding location, so a reader of the resulting introspection need not say 'the stored fields do not name them'.
criteria.evidence: The test an_unmet_criterion_and_a_major_finding_reach_the_prompt passes, but it does not go through the fake model or event_of_job. It feeds a hand-written string, 'title: reason' + verification_text(v), straight into user_prompt with a hand-built Event. crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs already has a scripted fake model that records every prompt it is sent (lines 32-60), and the change does not use it. So nothing shows that a stored rejected job's verification.json actually reaches the model's prompt. If the new push_str in event_of_job were deleted, every test would still pass.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: an entry under 'Changed' names the cause (`what` held only the title and outcome reason) and the fix, the caps, and the tests.

findings.summary: No test checks that event_of_job adds the verification text, or that a job with no verification keeps the old `what`
findings.evidence: All four new tests call verification_text or user_prompt directly. None builds a job record and calls event_of_job, so the root-cause fix, the wiring in event_of_job, could be removed without any test failing. Criterion 4's 'job without verification' shape and criterion 5's 'with the fake model' check are both missing. The scripted fake in crates/athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs already records prompts and could be used.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs, tests module (around lines 1494-1600) and event_of_job (around line 1174)

findings.summary: The changelog says the text 'is redacted with the rest of the prompt', but the prompt is not redacted
findings.evidence: In introspect.rs only the model's answer passes through redactor.redact_all (apply_answer, around line 1355). The user prompt goes to the driver as it is. The stored output_tail was already redacted when it was written (checks.rs:197), so the practical risk is low, but the sentence misdescribes the mechanism.

findings.summary: One line of the SYSTEM_PROMPT literal is much longer than the lines around it
findings.evidence: The line ending 'Choose the failure class: the id of a registry class that fits, or `new` with a name and a \' was not rewrapped.

summary: The change fails verification because two tested behaviours were never actually tested. The fix itself is right: when a rejected or failed job is introspected, event_of_job now adds that job's unmet criteria, blocker or major findings, and failed checks (under their own heading) to the text the model reads. The added text is capped, the system prompt tells the model that criteria and checks are different things, and the docs and changelog are updated within scope. The gaps are criteria 4 and 5. No test calls event_of_job, so there is no test for a job with no verification. Criterion 5's check through the fake model was replaced by a direct call to user_prompt with a hand-made string, so deleting the one line that wires the verification into `what` would leave every test passing. `cargo test -p athena-core introspect` passed (8 tests). I did not rerun the full suite, clippy or fmt; Athena reports they passed. A minor wording problem: the changelog says the new text is redacted with the rest of the prompt, but the prompt is not redacted, only the model's answer.
